---
title: "Topic 1 – Early Phosphorylation Response"
format: html
---

## 1. Load phosphoproteomics data

We use the STYH dataset, which includes phosphorylation searches for serine, threonine, tyrosine and histidine.

```{r}
source("../R/setup.R")
sites <- read_sites("STYH")

dim(sites)
names(sites)
```

## 2. Experimental groups

Check the number of observations per sample.

```{r}
sites %>%
  dplyr::count(genotype, medium, sample)
```

## 3. Missing phosphosite measurements

Calculate measurement coverage for the ancestral JE2 strain.

```{r}
sites %>%
  dplyr::filter(genotype == "anc") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(medium) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    total = dplyr::n(),
    measured = sum(!is.na(intensity)),
    missing = sum(is.na(intensity)),
    percent_measured = round(100 * measured / total, 1)
  )
```

## 4. Reproducibly detected phosphosites

Count phosphosites detected in at least two or all three replicates.

```{r}
sites %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    genotype == "anc",
    medium %in% c("TSB", "SNpulse")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(search, site_id, medium) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_detected = sum(!is.na(intensity)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(search, medium) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    sites_detected_2plus = sum(n_detected >= 2),
    sites_detected_all3 = sum(n_detected == 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## 5. Phosphosites reliably detected in both conditions

We identify phosphosites measured in at least 2 of 3 replicates in both TSB and SNpulse.

```{r}
site_overlap <- sites %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    genotype == "anc",
    medium %in% c("TSB", "SNpulse")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(search, site_id, medium) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_detected = sum(!is.na(intensity)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = medium,
    values_from = n_detected,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(TSB >= 2, SNpulse >= 2)

nrow(site_overlap)
```
**Interpretation:** Of the 469 phosphosites reproducibly detected in TSB and 262 in SNpulse, 200 were detected in at least 2 of 3 biological replicates in both conditions.

The prepared observed DEA analysis contains 170 unique phosphosites. The difference suggests additional filtering in the DEA pipeline, which still needs to be verified.


## 6. Load differential abundance analysis (DEA) results

The prepared phosphoproteomics DEA table contains statistical comparisons between experimental conditions. We initially focus on the ancestral JE2 strain (anc).

```{r}
dea_phospho <- read_dea("phospho_STYH")

dim(dea_phospho)
names(dea_phospho)
```

## 7. Compare early and long-term phosphorylation responses

We compare the 15-minute PASN exposure (SNpulse) with the long-term exposure (~15 h, SN).

We analyse observed measurements separately from limit-of-detection-imputed estimates.

Significance criteria:
- FDR < 0.05
- Absolute log2 fold change > 1

```{r}
phospho_summary <- dea_phospho %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    contrast %in% c(
      "TSB_vs_SNpulse_at_anc",
      "TSB_vs_SN_at_anc"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(contrast, estimate_type) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_rows = dplyr::n(),
    n_tested = sum(!is.na(FDR)),
    n_significant = sum(
      FDR < 0.05 & abs(diff) > 1,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    percent_significant = round(
      100 * n_significant / n_tested, 2
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

phospho_summary
```

## 8. Check unique phosphosites in the observed analysis

We verify that each row corresponds to a distinct phosphosite.

```{r}
dea_phospho %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    contrast == "TSB_vs_SNpulse_at_anc",
    estimate_type == "observed"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    rows = dplyr::n(),
    unique_sites = dplyr::n_distinct(site_id),
    unique_proteins = dplyr::n_distinct(protein_key)
  )
```

## 9. Identify significant phosphosites after 15 minutes

We identify phosphosites with statistically significant changes in the observed analysis.

For the contrast TSB_vs_SNpulse_at_anc:
- Negative diff: higher phosphosite signal after PASN exposure
- Positive diff: higher phosphosite signal in TSB

```{r}
early_phospho_hits <- dea_phospho %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    contrast == "TSB_vs_SNpulse_at_anc",
    estimate_type == "observed",
    FDR < 0.05,
    abs(diff) > 1
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    locus_tag,
    product,
    residue,
    position,
    diff,
    FDR
  )

early_phospho_hits
```

## 10. Preliminary interpretation

The observed phosphoproteomics analysis identified 3 significant phosphosites out of 170 tested sites (1.76%) after 15 minutes of PASN exposure.

The three sites are:

- B7H15_01690, S33: increased phosphosite signal after PASN exposure.
- B7H15_05655, T21: decreased phosphosite signal after PASN exposure.
- B7H15_14290 (IsaA), S194: increased phosphosite signal after PASN exposure.

The long-term observed analysis identified 18 significant sites out of 170 tested (10.59%).

These findings provide preliminary evidence of an early phosphorylation response, but the interpretation depends on the statistical model, detection reliability and possible changes in total protein abundance.

The comparison with total proteomics will be performed together with Person B.

## 11. Compare reproducibly detected sites with observed DEA sites

We compare the phosphosites passing our detection criterion (at least 2 of 3 replicates in both conditions) with those included in the observed DEA analysis.

```{r}
observed_sites <- dea_phospho %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    contrast == "TSB_vs_SNpulse_at_anc",
    estimate_type == "observed"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(site_id)

overlap_check <- site_overlap %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    reproducible_sites = dplyr::n_distinct(site_id),
    also_in_observed_dea = sum(site_id %in% observed_sites$site_id),
    not_in_observed_dea = sum(!site_id %in% observed_sites$site_id)
  )

overlap_check
```
## 12. Detection reliability of significant early phosphosites

We check whether the three significant phosphosites from the observed DEA analysis were detected in at least 2 of 3 replicates in both TSB and SNpulse.

```{r}
early_phospho_hits_check <- dea_phospho %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    contrast == "TSB_vs_SNpulse_at_anc",
    estimate_type == "observed",
    FDR < 0.05,
    abs(diff) > 1
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    reproducibly_detected = site_id %in% site_overlap$site_id
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    locus_tag,
    residue,
    position,
    diff,
    FDR,
    reproducibly_detected
  )

early_phospho_hits_check
```
## 13. Roadmap A – Statistical analysis of reproducible phosphosites

We follow the lecturer's Roadmap A to test phosphorylation changes after 15 minutes and approximately 15 hours of PASN exposure.

Only phosphosites detected in at least 2 of 3 replicates in both compared groups are included.

### 13.1 Normalisation

Phosphosite intensities are median-centred separately for each sample. This corrects for differences in overall phosphoproteomics signal, assuming that most sites remain unchanged.

```{r}
sites <- sites %>%
  dplyr::group_by(sample) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    log2_norm = log2_intensity -
      median(log2_intensity, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()
```

### 13.2 Statistical testing using limma

We use the lecturer's reproducible-site analysis with the limma package.

```{r}
library(limma)

compare_reproducible <- function(sites, group_a, group_b, min_per_group = 2) {
  x <- dplyr::filter(sites, group %in% c(group_a, group_b))

  keep <- x %>%
    dplyr::group_by(site_id, group) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      n = sum(!is.na(log2_norm)),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(site_id) %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      dplyr::n_distinct(group) == 2,
      all(n >= min_per_group)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::pull(site_id) %>%
    unique()

  wide <- x %>%
    dplyr::filter(site_id %in% keep) %>%
    dplyr::select(site_id, sample, log2_norm) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
      names_from = sample,
      values_from = log2_norm
    )

  m <- as.matrix(wide[, -1])
  rownames(m) <- wide$site_id

  grp <- factor(
    x$group[match(colnames(m), x$sample)],
    levels = c(group_a, group_b)
  )

  design <- model.matrix(~ grp)
  fit <- limma::eBayes(limma::lmFit(m, design))

  limma::topTable(fit, coef = 2, number = Inf) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("site_id") %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      site_id,
      contrast = paste0(group_a, "_vs_", group_b),
      diff = -logFC,
      p.value = P.Value,
      FDR = p.adjust(P.Value, "BH")
    )
}

res_a <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  compare_reproducible(sites, "anc_TSB", "anc_SN"),
  compare_reproducible(sites, "anc_TSB", "anc_SNpulse")
)
```

### 13.3 Summary of significant phosphorylation changes

We define significant changes using FDR < 0.1 and absolute log2 fold change > 1.

```{r}
roadmap_a_summary <- res_a %>%
  dplyr::group_by(contrast) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    sites_tested = dplyr::n(),
    significant_sites = sum(FDR < 0.1 & abs(diff) > 1),
    percent_significant = round(
      100 * significant_sites / sites_tested, 2
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

roadmap_a_summary
```

### 13.4 Significant early phosphosites

Identify phosphosites showing significant changes after 15 minutes.

```{r}
early_roadmap_a_hits <- res_a %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    contrast == "anc_TSB_vs_anc_SNpulse",
    FDR < 0.1,
    abs(diff) > 1
  )

early_roadmap_a_hits
```

### 13.5 Preliminary interpretation

Roadmap A identifies 2 significantly changed phosphosites among 200 tested sites (1.0%) after 15 minutes of PASN exposure.

After approximately 15 hours, 102 of 311 tested sites (32.8%) show significant changes.

These results indicate that an early phosphorylation response is detectable, but the proportion of significantly changed phosphosites is much higher after long-term exposure.

The two significant early sites are H15 and S33. Both show higher normalised phosphosite signals after PASN exposure.

Because phosphosite intensity can also depend on total protein abundance, these results do not directly establish changes in phosphorylation occupancy.

The final comparison with total proteomics will be performed together with Person B.


## 14. Identify proteins and localisation confidence of early phosphosites

We annotate the two significant early phosphosites identified by Roadmap A and examine their phosphorylation-site localisation probabilities.

```{r}
early_hits_annotated <- early_roadmap_a_hits %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    sites %>%
      dplyr::distinct(
        site_id, locus_tag, product, residue,
        position, best_loc_prob
      ),
    by = "site_id"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    site_id, locus_tag, product, residue,
    position, best_loc_prob, diff, FDR
  )

early_hits_annotated
```
